reasoning: Two acts, and no act absorbs the other. 'Деплой блин' is an instruction: the build is ready, shipping it is not checkpointed as anything, so it is new work with its own goal — the build is live. 'Запиши себе всегда деплой без моего подтверждения' is a decision in the skill's own sense: 'always' plus 'note this for yourself' settles a standing rule and a grant of authority that outlives today's deploy, and this is the case the skill spells out — recording only the standing rule loses the thing he actually wanted done today. The curse is tone, not a third act; it reports nothing new. Nothing was in flight for either to attach to — the withholding was a standing policy, not a tracked task — so the correction path does not apply and the decision earns its own home rather than a change to running work. Hence two separate pieces of work: either could ship or be cancelled without the other. The rule needs its one home named before a word of it is written, which is why documentation is touched; the deploy itself touches release. No spec author (behaviour is unchanged), no test author (no new evidence to choose), no verifier beyond the Director's own re-check that the build is actually live. One thing gets said before the sheet becomes a checkpoint: a blanket grant collides with the standing ground that a genuinely irreversible action outside git still stops for his word, so I state that and then proceed on his word either way.
